descriptionChirho: Physical movement upward to a place, ascending a mountain, hill, or city; traveling up geographically; going up to battle or to appear before God (Arabic صَعِدَ, Korean 올라가다/올라오다, Swahili panda/kupanda).

Rising of natural phenomena: sun rising, dawn breaking, plants sprouting, mist or vapor ascending, water springing up from the ground (Arabic طَلَعَ 'rise/appear', Korean 떠오르다, Swahili inuka/bubujika).
Causative sacrificial use: offering up burnt offerings and sacrifices upon an altar, causing the offering to ascend as smoke to God (Arabic أَصْعَدَ in ritual context, Korean 드리다/올리다, Swahili kutoa).

Causative movement of persons: bringing people up from one place to another, especially leading Israel up out of Egypt; raising someone up, fetching or summoning upward (Arabic أَصْعَدَ with personal objects, Korean 이끌어 올리다/데려가다, Swahili kupandisha/kuleta).
Causing the flame to go up on the lampstand: setting up, lighting, or kindling the lamps of the tabernacle or temple (Arabic رَفَعَ/أَصْعَدَ for lamps, Korean 켜다 'light/kindle', Swahili kuwasha).
Technical zoological use in dietary laws: bringing up the cud, ruminating, used to classify clean animals that chew the cud (Arabic الْمُجْتَرَّاتِ 'ruminants', Korean 올리는 것들 중에서, Swahili kuchea).
Passive or reflexive ascending: being lifted up, cloud rising from the tabernacle, withdrawing or departing upward (Arabic اِرْتَفَعَ/اِبْتَعَدَ, Korean 올라가다 passive, Swahili kuondoka/kuinuka).
